ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Federal Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing in the Financial Sector (AMLA, SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as substantially revised effective 1 January 2023 and 1 January 2024; Swiss Criminal Code (SR 311.0), Articles 305bis, 305ter and 260quinquies; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220), Articles 620-763 governing the Aktiengesellschaft, including the obligation to identify beneficial owners for the Commercial Register; Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411), including beneficial owner declaration provisions implementing the AMLA revision; Federal Act on the Embargo (SR 946.02); FINMA Circular 2023/03 on money laundering due diligence obligations of financial intermediaries.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Extract of Commercial Register of each non-Swiss corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry authority in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, plus certified German/French/Italian translation where the original is not in an official Swiss language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies of all shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent public registrar in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or full consular legalization where the country of origin is not a Hague Convention Contracting State; certified translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Vollmacht/Prokura) authorizing the Swiss incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and, where applicable, consular legalization chain through the Swiss representation abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of no bankruptcy or debt enforcement proceedings for each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cantonal Debt Enforcement Office (Betreibungsamt) for Swiss residents, or equivalent home-state judicial or registry authority for foreign directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Betreibungsregisterauszug, or foreign equivalent authenticated by Hague Apostille / consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence under AMLA Article 4 and FINMA Circular 2023/03; compulsory screening of all shareholders, directors and UBOs against the OFAC SDN list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) designated sanctions measures under the Swiss Embargo Act, and the Swiss domestic criminal register. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced monitoring, written approval by the compliance officer, and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification covering the paid-in minimum share capital of CHF 50,000. Screening must be completed prior to execution of the notarial deed of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Zentraler Firmenindex (Central Business Name Index), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Schweizerisches Handelsregisteramt) under Articles 940-957 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and the HRegV
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name must comply with Article 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations: it must be in the Latin alphabet, written in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian or Romansh), must not be misleading or offend public interests, must be distinguishable from all existing registered names, and must contain the legal form suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (in French or Italian: 'Société Anonyme' / 'SA'). Non-Latin script components require verifiable transliteration into Latin characters; the name must be reserved and cleared in the language of the incorporating canton.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Cantonal or municipal names without prior written consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written objection (Einsprache) with the competent cantonal commercial register office within 10 days of the rejection notice, attaching a revised name proposal and supporting justification. If the objection is denied, an administrative appeal (Beschwerde) may be lodged with the competent cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht) within 30 days of the objection decision. A further appeal lies to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) within 30 days. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately file a new name application with a corrected proposal; the Zefix name search must be re-run to confirm distinctiveness and absence of conflicting registered rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. A pure mailbox or correspondence-only virtual office is not acceptable for AG registration; the registered seat must be the actual administrative seat (Sitz) as stated in the articles of association. Licensed domiciliation service providers may offer registered-office arrangements in certain cantons, but genuine commercial substance is required for Swiss tax residence and for the statutory marine bunkering license. For ISIC 5222 offshore refueling activity, a physical operational office with verifiable management presence is recommended in a commercial canton such as Basel-Stadt, Geneva, Ticino or Zurich.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced on-site inspections: approximately 35% within the first 12 months of operation, elevated by the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier, the required statutory license, and the involvement of FINMA/SRO supervision of financial intermediaries; the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG/FOCBS) and cantonal explosives and environmental safety authorities may also conduct unannounced site visits for marine fuel handling operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), Part II, Arts. 620–763; especially Arts. 626–633 (formation, capital and escrow), Art. 643 (registered shares), Art. 716a–716b (board powers), and Art. 727 (mandatory audit thresholds).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton, accessed through the central Swiss Commercial Register (Zefix); final publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/FOSC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised public deed of incorporation with articles of association (Statuten), filed as a sworn commercial register registration application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: AG minimum nominal capital is CHF 100,000; at least CHF 50,000 (50%) must be actually paid up before registration. The paid-in amount must be deposited in a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) held by a Swiss bank and evidenced by a bank certificate to the notary; if the deed requires full payment, the entire CHF 100,000 remains blocked until the board obtains free control after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, ADOPTED: 1. The incorporation deed is approved; the subscribers subscribe for the registered share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100 registered shares of CHF 1,000, fully paid into the blocked formation escrow account per Article 633 of the Swiss Code of Obligations. 2. The registered office of the Company is fixed at the corporate address stated in the deed, and all implementing administrative acts are ratified. 3. The Board of Directors, composed of three natural persons, is appointed for a three-year term, and the Chair and Secretary are elected from among the directors with unlimited signatory authority. 4. The Chair is authorized, jointly with the Secretary, to file the incorporation with the Commercial Register and to arrange the initial general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank selected for the company in formation; the escrow arrangement must satisfy the corporate notary and Commercial Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a pre-registration banker's account in the name of the future AG and deposit the subscribed share capital into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto). The bank must issue a written blocked-account certificate confirming that the capital is available and irrevocably reserved until the company is registered and the board has taken office. Maintain source-of-funds documentation for AML/KYC purposes.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (Statuten)
Valid passport or identity document of every subscriber
AML/KYC forms and source-of-wealth declaration
Board composition statement and powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the account opening or the certificate wording, submit supplementary source-of-funds evidence or transfer the escrow to another Swiss bank; the certificate must be reissued until it matches the notary's formal requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarise the Deed of Incorporation and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss civil-law notary public in the canton of the registered office (Kantonsnotariat).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary together with all subscribers and specially-instructed board members. Present the final articles, share subscription list and the blocked-account certificate. The notary reads the deed, verifies the identities, obtains signatures, and executes the public deed. The deed records name, domicile, purpose, share capital, share categories, board powers and auditor.
required_dossiers: Passport or identity card of each incorporator
Blocked-account certificate from the Swiss escrow bank
Final signed articles of association in two copies
Share subscription and board appointment statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, execute a corrective notarial rider or re-execute the deed the same day after fixing inconsistencies; if the paid-up capital is deficient, replenish the escrow account and obtain a new bank certificate before signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Entry in the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), coordinated through the central Zefix electronic register portal on behalf of the Swiss Federal Commercial Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarised deed and the electronic registration form to the competent cantonal commercial register. The register examines incorporation legality, name eligibility, available capacity, capital, purpose and representative authority. Once admitted, the entry is created, a Swiss UID is assigned, and the registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Notarised deed of incorporation and articles
Official registration form signed by the board with notarised signatures
Escrow certificate of paid-up share capital
Board resolution on the Chair, directors and auditor
Formal declaration of formation expenses and domicile consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a deficiency notice or suspension, respond in writing within the statutory period with corrected documents; if a name conflict occurs, amend the articles by notarial resolution and re-file; replacement filing fees are not assessed if the defect is cured under the original application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for UID, Direct Tax, VAT and Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Cantonal Tax Administration and the cantonal AHV/compensation office, with automatic UID assignment from the Federal Statistical Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Commercial Register admission, collect the central business identification (UID) number from Zefix. Register the AG for cantonal corporate income tax and municipal taxes at the commercial port/corporate seat; apply to the Federal Tax Administration for VAT (MWST) if taxable turnover reaches the CHF 100,000 threshold; register as an employer with the AHV compensation office and accident insurance carrier.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt or UID confirmation
VAT registration questionnaire (Form 080A) where applicable
Employer registration form for social security (AHV/IV/EO)
Tax declaration of economic activity and place of management
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security registrations are delayed, submit a written rectification request to ESTV and the compensation office with the Commercial Register excerpt; retroactive registration may be granted only after written confirmation of the effective incorporation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm SHAB Publication and Constitute Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/FOSC) publication service; board of directors for internal corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the official publication record after commercial registration and download the certified excerpt. Convene the first post-registration board meeting to approve the share register, beneficial-owner register, signature specimens, bank account control release, and management contracts. Retain all minutes, registers and sealed statutory books at the registered office.
required_dossiers: SHAB/FOSC publication proof or certified excerpt
Board minutes of the post-registration meeting
Share register and beneficial-owner register
Authorised signatory list and specimen signature forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication is factually incorrect or the UID cannot be verified, file a request for correction with the Commercial Register Office; amend the share register and beneficial-owner register before any share transfer or voting-rights change.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade Licensing Office (Gewerbeamt/Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) in the port canton, coordinated with the Swiss Federal Office for National Economic Supply (FONES/BWL), the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security for excise-suspended marine fuels, and the Basel Rhine port authority for berth and bunkering-station concessions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Cantonal Permit for Commercial Storage, Handling and Supply of Marine Fuel, together with the Port Operating Licence for Bunkering Dock or Floating Fuel-Supply Station (Bunkerlizenz).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU/OFEV) and the competent cantonal environmental protection department.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) under the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV) is mandatory for new or substantially enlarged fuel storage terminals and pier installations with storage capacity above the statutory thresholds; smaller bunkering stations and transfer points are subject to prior environmental registration and compatibility inspection by the canton.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Federal Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV): oil-water separator effluent hydrocarbon index not exceeding 5 mg/l; no oily waste or bilge discharge into surface waters; VOC recovery or vapour-transfer efficiency at least 95% during bunkering; fuel spills to be captured by drip trays, containment booms and emergency spill kits; sludge, filters and contaminated residues must be removed by a licensed waste disposal operator under the Federal Waste Ordinance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal Fire Police (Feuerpolizei) certificate of fire-safety compliance to VKF/AEAI protection codes; structural load and pier stability inspection under Swiss SIA standards for all tank, hose and dock installations; SUVA occupational-safety clearance and accident-insurance coverage for personnel handling hazardous marine fuels, including explosion-protection zoning, gas detection, PPE and an activation procedure for emergency response and civil-defense containment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); sole software portal: www.estv.admin.ch and the eService VAT filing portal (eservices.estv.admin.ch). Cantonal and municipal tax administrations administer income and capital taxes at sub-national level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is incorporated by public notarial deed and entered in the Commercial Register (Handelsregister); the Federal Statistical Office (BFS) then issues the enterprise identification number (UID/IDE/IID). VAT registration is filed separately with the ESTV through the eService portal within 30 days of commencing taxable activity; the ESTV assigns the VAT suffix MWST/IVA/TVA to the UID (format: CHE-123.456.789 MWST). Foreign entities not established in Switzerland may either obtain a direct UID/VAT ID from the ESTV or appoint a Swiss fiscal representative in order to file VAT returns, subject to the statutory thresholds and place-of-supply rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections relevant to the shipping-bunkering AG include: VAT group election (consolidated VAT registration of closely held entities under Art. 21 LTVA); participation deduction election for dividend and capital-gain income on qualifying participations (Art. 69 DBG); election to maintain capital contribution reserves as distributable Swiss-reserve equity (Art. 5s DBG); and the election to treat domestic branches or co-entrepreneurial joint venture activities as independent taxable units. Hybrid mismatch legislation implementing OECD BEPS Action 2 has been in force since 1 January 2020 and disallows passthrough or hybrid mismatch election outcomes that create double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto) under the Federal VAT Act (LTVA/Mehrwertsteuergesetz of 12 June 2009)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 of annual worldwide taxable turnover for Swiss-established businesses; for non-established foreign businesses, CHF 100,000 of annual turnover derived from taxable services performed in Switzerland, with deliveries of goods located in Switzerland triggering immediate registration without a monetary threshold; small businesses may elect voluntary registration under Art. 7 LTVA; the 8.1% standard rate applies from 1 January 2024 (increased from 7.7%; reduced rate 2.6%; accommodation rate 3.7%).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time State-operated fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate exists in Switzerland. Invoices must contain mandatory statutory content under Art. 37 LTVA (supplier name/address, UID, invoice date, nature of supply, consideration exclusive of tax, VAT rate and tax amount); eBill and QR-bills are compulsory for electronic supplier payments to Swiss federal and cantonal authorities and are standard in B2B practice, but tax clearance is effected exclusively through periodic VAT returns submitted via the ESTV eService portal. Bunkering operators may issue electronic PDF/XML invoices without pre-authorisation, provided the mandatory content is complete and the VAT number of the customer is stated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Art. 53(1) LTVA, the 0% rate applies to supplies of goods physically exported from Switzerland into a foreign customs territory and to services directly related to export or import, including international transport. For marine bunkering, fuel and lubricants delivered into the bunker tanks of a vessel engaged in international merchant navigation qualify as zero-rated export-like supplies provided the operator demonstrates: (i) the vessel departs on a verifiable foreign itinerary, (ii) delivery takes place under Swiss customs custody or within the free-port/transit framework, and (iii) the product is intended exclusively for consumption in international navigation. Supplies to vessels operating solely on domestic Swiss waterways (e.g., Lake Geneva or the Rhine within Swiss territorial limits) remain taxable at the standard 8.1% rate; the burden of proving export eligibility rests on the supplier on pain of retrospective assessment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss Customs Main/E-DEC declaration) evidencing exit from the Swiss customs territory
Bill of Lading or international waybill showing foreign destination port and vessel identity
Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) signed by the vessel's chief engineer stating the quantity and grade of fuel delivered
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 evidencing payment receipt from the foreign counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ESTV and the Federal Customs Administration (Oberzolldirektion) routinely audit export zero-rating and require the supplier to retain the complete documentary bundle for at least 10 years. Missing, false, or late documentary evidence triggers retrospective clawback of the 0% rate with default interest at 4.5% per annum. Intentional tax evasion (Art. 76 LTVA) exposes the taxable person to a fine of up to three times the evaded tax (one time where the evaded tax is below CHF 50,000), confiscation of the goods, and criminal prosecution of responsible officers; negligent under-declaration (Art. 77 LTVA) attracts fines and administrative penalties, and knowingly issuing false export or BDN certificates may lead to a fine of up to CHF 10,000 per document plus loss of the right to deduct input VAT and suspension of the bunkering licence under ISIC 5222.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; Schweizerische Nationalbank/Banque nationale suisse/Banca Nazionale Svizzera)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII and OECD standards. No exchange controls, prior approvals, or quantitative restrictions apply to cross-border payments, profit remittances, dividend repatriation, or shareholder loans. The 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends is imposed at the tax level, not the FX level, and may be reduced or eliminated by a double tax treaty. Bunkering proceeds in USD, EUR, or CHF can be held, transferred, and converted freely without SNB authorisation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Switzerland imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds or to convert foreign currency earnings to CHF. Bunker fuel exporters and service providers may retain USD/EUR revenues in Swiss or offshore accounts and freely decide on conversion timing and hedging.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium. Switzerland's FinTech Licence regime (Art. 1b Swiss Banking Act) permits a non-bank fintech to take public sight deposits up to CHF 100 million without a full banking licence. However, this licence is not an EMI passport, and Switzerland is not part of the EU/EEA passporting network. A Swiss-domiciled AG engaged in bunkering will generally require a traditional bank for SWIFT interoperability and for Standby LC issuance; a fintech EMI may be used only for ancillary pre-funded employee expenses or secondary clearing, not as a primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Digital/video KYC and remote onboarding are permitted under FINMA AML-Ordinance provisions for domestic AGs with Swiss-resident directors. Nevertheless, in practice tier-1 Swiss banks require an in-person or video-verified interview with the operational director and ultimate beneficial owners before account activation, especially for marine-bunkering (Medium-Risk Enhanced). A physical visit to the bank in Switzerland is mandatory for non-resident UBOs unless the bank has an existing private-banking relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions exposure in bunkering value chain: vessels flagged in high-risk jurisdictions, counterparties associated with embargoed states, or fuel supplied to ships transiting sanctioned waters.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Vessel IMO number, certificate of registry, charter party agreement, end-user certificate, SBRE (Suspicious Bunkering and Related Equipment) screening result, UN/EU/OFAC sanctions screening report, vessel insurance policy, and transaction-level confirmation that the vessel is engaged exclusively in international trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment opacity: third-party payer/beneficiary structures, prepaid cards, or cash-like instruments used for bunker fuel settlement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contractual payment terms, audited financial statements, board resolution approving the treasury policy, bank statements, sworn declaration of the commercial parties, POP (Proof of Product) and POD (Proof of Delivery) documents, and an explanatory note demonstrating the commercial necessity of the payment structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance of the Swiss AG: no local operations, no payroll or office, or UBO ownership routed through shell jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for Swiss premises, payroll and social insurance records (AHV), UBO declaration and register of shareholders, notarised constitutive documents, capital adequacy evidence, statutory auditor report, and a business plan substantiating real operations in the marine bunkering and refueling industry.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections and shareholder loans to the Swiss AG must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 with Swiss balance-of-payments purpose code '110' (equity) or '660' (short-term shareholder loan), accompanied by a board resolution, updated commercial register extract, and source-of-funds declaration. The receiving bank will verify that the remitter is the named shareholder and that no anonymous or third-party transit account is used. For capital contributions paid into a Band-Escrow, provisional account wording must be clear to avoid misinterpretation as trade proceeds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements rely on SWIFT MT103 for advance payments and open-account bunker purchases, SWIFT MT202 for interbank liquidity transfers, and Commercial Standby Letters of Credit issued under UCP 600 or ISP98 to secure performance bonds for bunker supply contracts. For bulk fuel procurement, a Documentary Letter of Credit with transferable drawdown conditions is acceptable. For EUR/CHF settlements, SEPA CT (MT103-equivalent) payments are suitable. All payments must reference the appropriate Swiss purpose codes and include an invoice allocation to avoid Customs and VAT audit triggers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CHF/USD, CHF/EUR and CHF/GBP forward contracts with tenors up to 24 months
FX options on major convertible pairs (European-style, settlement by margin)
Cross-currency swaps (fixed/floating, MTM and collateralised under ISDA CSA)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or thinly traded currencies as a non-CHF hedge, executed through FINMA-licensed or EU-licensed dealing counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return for legal entities (Steuererklärung/Formular NLP) covering federal, cantonal and communal taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration of registered seat plus Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March following the financial year end for calendar-year accounts, with routine administrative extension to 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5% p.a.; procedural fines up to CHF 10,000; estimated assessment on non-filing is reversible only upon filing within 30 days

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT annual return under the annual accounting scheme (in respect of ship bunkering and refuelling services where annual Swiss turnover does not exceed CHF 5,523,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, VAT Division (ESTV/ISD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual VAT return within 60 days after close of tax period; quarter-settled taxpayers file within 60 days after each calendar quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest at 4.5%; administrative fine up to 10% of tax at risk if negligent and up to 33⅓% if intentionally evasive; criminal referral for continued evasion

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual wage declaration and AHV/IV/EO social security contribution settlement applicable to all crew members and shore employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compulsory compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) assigned to the employer's AHV number
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Wage declaration due by 31 January; final contribution settlement due by 31 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest of 4%–5%; administrative surcharges; fines under Swiss Old-Age and Survivors Insurance supervisory law; loss of public tender eligibility for material non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting approving annual financial statements, budget, and discharge (Entlastung) of board of directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No filing to a public authority; shareholders' meeting resolution is recorded in the company minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months from balance sheet date (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered convocation upon shareholder request; directors face civil liability for damages; criminal default penalties under the Swiss Code of Obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements with the commercial register and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) publication, applicable where the AG is subject to ordinary audit or is a listed company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt/Registre du commerce) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months from balance sheet date, accompanied by the audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive directive with recurrent penal fine; directors personally liable for damages; persistent non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of port/municipal commercial operating licence for ship bunkering and refuelling (Gewerbebewilligung/Handelspatent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal/municipal trade authority and surface port authority of the operating harbour (e.g., Basel-Stadt Rheinhafen)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal on or before 31 December or on the fixed date set by the issuing authority; fee follows the municipal tariff schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension or withdrawal of operating licence; prohibition of port access; per-day coercive fines; unlicensed bunkering activity triggers criminal proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit is mandatory when two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: CHF 20,000,000 total assets, CHF 40,000,000 net turnover, or 250 FTE employees; companies not meeting these criteria require a limited audit; audit may be fully waived only if the AG has fewer than 10 FTE employees and all shareholders consent (Art. 727–727a CO)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (Art. 957–963b CO); Swiss GAAP FER is the common presentation framework for statutory purposes; IFRS is permitted for statutory reporting and mandatory for Swiss-listed issuers

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no public UBO register and imposes no annual UBO confirmation form; beneficial ownership must be identified and documented under FINMA CDB 20 anti-money-laundering rules, with marine bunkering classified as medium-risk enhanced due diligence; share transfers must be recorded promptly in the share register (Aktienbuch), and CDB 20 records must be retained for at least 10 years after termination of the business relationship
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch / registre des actionnaires)
Register of Directors and Managing Directors (as filed in the commercial register, kept at registered office)
Minute book of shareholder meetings and board resolutions (Protokollbuch)
General ledger, journal, and annual financial statements in accordance with Art. 958f CO

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 1,000 – 4,000 p.a. (approx. USD 1,100 – 4,500) depending on canton and service level
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 4,000 – 25,000 (approx. USD 4,500 – 28,000): limited audit CHF 3,000 – 8,000; ordinary audit CHF 12,000 – 30,000 for a mid-size bunkering entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal statutory rate 8.5% of post-tax profit (approx. 7.83% pre-tax), combined with cantonal and communal profit taxes yielding a typical effective headline rate of 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton; Zug approx. 11.9%–15.1%, Zurich approx. 19.7%, Geneva approx. 21.0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Beneficial regimes: participation exemption (substantial dividend/capital-gain exemption for qualifying participations), patent box (qualifying IP income reduced by 10%–90% per canton), R&D super-deduction up to 150% in certain cantons, deemed interest deduction for excess cash (some cantons), and international shipping/bunkering profit exemption provisions for strictly qualifying Swiss shipping enterprises (Art. 64 LIFD).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal Direct Tax Return for Legal Entities (Form M for AG/SA) integrated with cantonal/communal tax return; e-filing via the canton's authorised eTax platform or certified commercial tax software using the eCH standardised XML interface (approved by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration ESTV/AFC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due six months after the balance sheet date; for calendar-year companies the general cantonal deadline is 30 September or 31 October depending on the canton; written extension applications are available for justified cause.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, registered office, Swiss UID (IDE-CH identifier), ownership structure, board of directors, auditor details and share capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must list their address and foreign tax residence code; the Swiss AG reports as a resident taxpayer in Switzerland, not as branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assets, liabilities and shareholders' equity at the beginning of the fiscal year; reconciliation with prior year closing balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG wholly owned by non-residents, the opening balance sheet must be complete and independent; no consolidation into foreign parent balance sheet is permitted in the Swiss return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Closing assets, liabilities, equity, provisions and accruals at the fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent guarantees or financing arrangements must be disclosed; arm's length terms for capital contributions and shareholder loans must be substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C: Profit and Loss Account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue (bunkering sales, marine fuel procurement, handling fees, ancillary logistics), cost of goods sold, personnel costs, depreciation, financial expenses and overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenues from foreign-flag vessels must be segregated from domestic bunkering to analyse treaty exposure and possible international shipping exemption claim.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D: Net Profit before Taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before Swiss federal, cantonal and communal income taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG's taxable net profit is the full company net profit; no PE remittance deduction is allowed to non-resident shareholders unless specifically derived from a permanent establishment allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E: Tax Reconciliation / Non-Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-business expenses, excessive interest or royalties, provisions not accepted for tax purposes, hidden profit distributions and political/charitable non-deductibles; deduction of loss carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Strict arm's length transfer pricing adjustments (fuel acquisition margins, intercompany management fees, interest rates) must be included; related-party transactions with parent/sister entities require supporting comparables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable federal and cantonal/communal base after tax adjustments and loss carry-forwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the AG qualifies as a mixed domestic company or as a shipping enterprise, special allocation factors must be shown; otherwise 100% of world-wide taxable income of the Swiss AG is subject to Swiss tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a procedural fine (Verspätungszuschlag) up to CHF 10,000 per canton, an extension interest due, and a tax-assessed penalty if authorities issue a summary assessment; intentionally submitting incomplete or inaccurate tax returns entails a fine up to 100% of the escaped tax and further criminal prosecution under Art. 175 DBG (LIFD).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory Swiss withholding tax on dividends paid to all shareholders, including non-resident shareholders; domestic Swiss shareholders may receive full refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from DTA reduction, the non-resident parent/beneficial owner must submit to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV-AFC) Form 82/85 (formal application for partial repayment or relief-at-source), together with an original or digitally certified Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty jurisdiction, documentary proof of beneficial ownership (form A), confirmation of the underlying shareholding period (usually minimum 2 years for treaty-shopping safeguards), and relevant share register excerpts; processing generally requires 2–6 months. If DTA relief was not granted at source, a deferred refund may be filed within the statutory limitation period (generally 3 years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss domestic law imposes no withholding tax on IP royalties; Dutch? Interest is likewise not subject to Swiss withholding tax when paid as ordinary commercial loan interest, although Swiss WHT of 35% applies to interest paid on bonds, money-market instruments issued by Swiss companies, and interest credited by Swiss banks. Under most Swiss DTA treaties, interest and royalties may be taxed at 0%–5%; anti-abuse clauses (beneficial owner, LOBS, principal purpose test) apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss tax law does not prescribe a statutory mandatory Local File/Master File, but administrative practice requires contemporaneous TP documentation whenever the Swiss entity's related-party cross-border transaction volume exceeds CHF 5 million in any fiscal year or when a tax adjustment risk is material; a Master File is required where the global group's net turnover exceeds CHF 50 million. The documentation must substantiate arm's length results per OECD TP Guidelines.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply Gulf-type Economic Substance Regulations, but it imposes a substantive economic activity requirement through Art. 58 LIFD and international treaty jurisprudence: a Swiss AG must have actual offices, qualified employees, real decision-making power, bank accounts, and genuine fuel procurement/refuelling logistics in Switzerland. For bunkering activities, legal title to fuel, cargo ownership, invoicing procedures, safety/labour operations must be performed by the Swiss entity. Failure of economic substance leads to denial of treaty benefits under the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) Principal Purpose Test and permits cantonal/FTA substance auditing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Understatement (Federal and Cantonal Direct Tax)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating taxable income by back-dating bunkering invoices, excluding retrospective rebates or trade discounts, inflating cost of bunker fuel, using sham intermediary suppliers, or shifting Swiss AG profits artificially to a foreign group company without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 174–175 DBG/LIFD, intentional tax evasion triggers a fine equal to up to 100% of the evaded tax plus a procedural fine; in aggravated cases or where the evaded tax exceeds CHF 30,000, the court may impose a mandatory compliance penalty and publish the judgment; unpaid federal and cantonal tax interest accrues at 4.5% annual. In addition, a false or fraudulent electronic tax return subjects the AG to an administrative summary assessment and loss of all loss carry-forward claims for the manipulated year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members, the CEO and signatories who knowingly sign false tax returns expose themselves to joint and several personal criminal fines; the court may impose imprisonment up to 3 years under Swiss criminal law (Art. 146/251 StGB) for documentary forgery/fraud. Directors are personally liable for resulting unpaid taxes if they fail to file compulsory balance-sheet reports of losses (Art. 754, 725 OR); travel bans may be imposed under fiscal enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Offshore Shell Company / Sham Substance in Bunkering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a Swiss AG with only a nominal registered office, no operational staff, no commercial control of marine fuel contracts, no physical bunkering or storage activity in Switzerland, and with the practical purpose of obtaining Swiss DTA benefits and bank accounts while actual decision-making and profit generation occurs in a no-tax or low-tax jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration re-characterises the entity as a sham PE or de facto foreign controlled resident; treaty benefits are denied (MLI PPT), withholding tax at 35% is withheld or clawed back on all profit repatriations; cantonal authorities may order dissolution of the company under Art. 731b OR for non-existence of legal seat and organisation; the company is deemed to lack the necessary charter/settlement place, and fines up to CHF 100,000 may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors' personal criminal liability arises where they knowingly facilitate a sham structure (corporate veil piercing); under Art. 754 OR, the FTA and creditors can sue directors for compensation if the company is unable to pay its tax debts. Directors and shadow directors face travel bans, asset attachment and, in cross-border tax fraud cases, extradition risk; imprisonment from one to five years under Swiss criminal law for forgery, fraud and money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering in Bunker Payments and Sanctions Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or third-party payments without beneficial ownership disclosure for marine fuel refuelling, using the Swiss AG bank account to move funds in support of sanctioned operators, Iranian/Venezuelan-origin fuel trading, or creating split invoices to disguise the true counterparty and evade Swiss or UN sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) and Criminal Code Art. 305bis, acts of money laundering carry imprisonment of up to three years and/or a fine up to CHF 500,000; aggravated cases (such as participation in a criminal organisation) attract up to five years' imprisonment; commercial-scale violations of UN/Swiss economic embargos under Art. 6 of the Federal Embargo Act may lead to imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to CHF 2 million; the AG can be classified as a non-complying financial intermediary and lose its banking access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who fail to perform adequate KYC and transaction monitoring may be held personally criminally liable as principals of the money-laundering offence; they can be subject to immediate travel bans, bank account freezes, and confiscation of personal assets; civil liability arises under Art. 41 CO with joint and several indemnification of the company's losses; imprisonment up to five years and permanent disqualification from serving as director of a Swiss AG apply in serious cases.
